body:
Soojin Lee: Need a decision on the headline slide copy before DES-618 locks templates. Current options are:
A) “Production economics for LLM inference”
B) “Unified inference across hosted, dedicated, private”
C) “Predictable inference: latency, cost, reliability”

Goal: 1 line that anchors the whole demo. What do we want the room to remember? Drop edits + vote w/ :one: :two: :three:.

Camila Reyes: My take: A is strongest / most differentiated vs generic “platform”. But “economics” can feel finance-y if it’s the *first* slide.
Copy tweak: “Production-grade economics for LLM inference” (signals reliability + cost).
Vote :one: (with that tweak)

Dylan Brooks: +1 that B is accurate but reads like a feature list.
If we keep B, I’d shorten: “One runtime. Any deployment.” (then subhead w/ hosted/dedicated/private).
Vote :three: for “Predictable inference…” bc it tees up SLOs + routing + cost tooling.

Alex Martinez: Thinking about devs: they want “why you vs vLLM + some glue?”
“Production economics” is good if we immediately show levers (batching/caching/quant) in the first 5 minutes.
If we don’t, it’s a promise we have to earn.
Vote :three: (and we can reinforce “economics” on slide 4/5)

Stephanie Nguyen: From the field: execs perk up on “cost + reliability”. “Unified inference” feels like infra plumbing unless they’ve already been burned.
If we’re trying to hook in 30 seconds: “Predictable inference” is the least polarizing.
Vote :three:

Markus Klein: From demo flow standpoint, we *do* hit unit economics early (token breakdown + batching toggle). So A is defensible.
But agree on the “finance-y” risk.
What about: “Ship faster with predictable LLM inference” (then bullets: latency, cost, reliability, any deployment)
Vote between :one:/:three: — leaning :three: for now.

Camila Reyes: Another micro-edit for :three::
“Predictable LLM inference: latency, cost, reliability”
(Keep “LLM” so it doesn’t read like generic inference.)

Renee Sullivan: +1 to explicitly say LLM.
Also “production economics” has been confusing in a couple rehearsals (“are you a billing product?”).
If we pick A, we should add a subhead that clarifies: “Optimize cost without trading off latency/reliability.”
Vote :three:

Soojin Lee: Tally so far:
:one: Camila
:three: Dylan, Alex, Stephanie, Renee (+ Markus leaning)

If we go with :three:, do we still want “unified inference” anywhere up top (headline/subhead) so Private/Dedicated folks feel seen?

Dylan Brooks: Suggest layout:
Headline: “Predictable LLM inference”
Subhead: “Latency + cost control, across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments”
Then 3 icons.

Camila Reyes: That’s good. Keeps B as supporting proof instead of the main claim.

Markus Klein: Works for the talk track too. Lets SE say: “No matter where you need to run it, you get the same knobs + observability.”

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Also helps us swap variants (enterprise-first can flip the subhead emphasis without rewriting headline).

Soojin Lee: Ok decision: headline = “Predictable LLM inference”
Subhead = “Latency + cost control, across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments”

Action: Camila can you push copy edit into the working outline + tag DES-618? I’ll update the canonical deck JSON + talk track transitions.

Camila Reyes: Yup. Will update Drive outline + ping design. :thumbsup:

Alex Martinez: If we use “Latency + cost control” can we avoid “Optimize” as a noun on later slides? People think it’s a separate product.
Maybe “Cost/performance toolkit” instead of “Optimize” in spoken track.

Soojin Lee: Noted. I’ll flag in speaker notes: say “cost/perf controls” first, then “Redwood Optimize (toolkit)” only if they ask.

Camila Reyes: Updated in outline. Commented w/ exact strings + approved variants for 20-min exec version.
Link: https://drive.google.com/…/demo-deck-outline-working (comment thread on slide 1)

Soojin Lee: Perfect. Locking this. Thanks all.
